subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The Earth's crust is broken into large sections called:
questions.explain: Tectonic plates move slowly on the semi-molten mantle below.

options: Plates move together and one is subducted
questions.explain: Oceanic crust is subducted beneath continental crust, causing earthquakes and volcanoes.

options: Plates move apart and new crust forms
questions.explain: Magma rises to form new crust as plates separate (e.g. mid-ocean ridges).

options: Stack on top of each other
questions.explain: Conservative boundaries cause earthquakes as plates slide past each other.

questions.q: The point beneath the surface where an earthquake originates is the:
questions.explain: The focus is underground; the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above it.

questions.q: The point on the surface directly above an earthquake's focus is the:
questions.explain: The epicentre usually experiences the strongest shaking.

options: Immediate impacts such as buildings collapsing
questions.explain: Primary effects happen instantly; secondary effects (fires, tsunamis, disease) follow.

questions.q: A tsunami is an example of a ___ effect of an undersea earthquake.
questions.explain: Tsunamis are secondary effects triggered by the primary event.

questions.q: Volcanoes and earthquakes are mostly found:
options: In the middle of plates only
questions.explain: Most tectonic hazards occur where plates meet.

questions.q: The 'three Ps' of reducing earthquake risk are prediction, protection and:
questions.explain: Prediction, protection (e.g. earthquake-proof buildings) and preparation reduce impacts.

options: Reducing collapse and saving lives during shaking

questions.q: People continue to live in tectonic hazard zones because of:
options: Fertile volcanic soils, resources, tourism or family ties
questions.explain: Benefits and attachments can outweigh perceived risks.

options: Search and rescue and emergency aid
Improving building codes for the future
questions.explain: Immediate responses save lives; long-term responses focus on recovery and planning.

questions.q: Earthquakes occur at plate boundaries because:
options: Stress builds as plates move and is suddenly released
questions.explain: Friction locks plates until stress is released as an earthquake.

questions.q: A lower-income country often suffers worse earthquake impacts than a higher-income country because it:
options: May have weaker buildings and fewer resources to respond
questions.explain: Wealth affects building quality, preparation and the capacity to respond.

questions.q: To reduce future earthquake deaths, a city should invest in:
options: Building codes, education drills and emergency planning
questions.explain: Protection and preparation are the most effective long-term measures.

specSource: Eduqas GCSE Geography A specification; Tectonic landscapes and hazards
